newsitem.title: GERMANY: Building slump hits Jan German industry output.
newsitem.headline: Building slump hits Jan German industry output.

text.p: German industrial output fell in January by 1.7 percent from December, with the fall in overall output caused by a dramatic 25 percent slump in construction activity, Economics Ministry data showed on Wednesday.
Stripping out construction, industry production would have risen by 1.3 percent in January, a ministry spokeswoman said in response to an inquiry.

The ministry said general weakness in the building sector was only partly to blame for the fall. It was compounded by unusually cold weather and changes to bad weather payments for idle building workers which were little used by companies.
Also, the ending of favourable write-off opportunities at the end of 1996 caused many projects to be brought forward to before the end of the year, the ministry added.
January's industry output was, however, up 1.7 percent on a year earlier, and a broader comparison of the latest two months against the previous two showed a gain of 0.5 percent.
In western Germany, January production fell by 0.5 percent on December and was up 1.2 percent on the same month a year earlier.
Output in the former communist east, however, was down a sharp 13.4 percent but up 2.7 percent on a year ago. Building in the region slumped by a staggering 35.7 percent.
